graph.title: Button Mouse Control (Arduino Leonardo, five pushbuttons)
notes: Step 1 parts were kept. Only the labels changed: the circuit image and schematic put pin 6 on the leftmost button and pin 2 on the rightmost, so btn1 is on pin 6 and btn5 is on pin 2. Step 1 had this the other way round.
Button-to-pin mapping follows the image: btn1=pin 6 (click), btn2=pin 5, btn3=pin 4, btn4=pin 3, btn5=pin 2.

Each pushbutton spans the centre gap with legs in two columns. Side 1 (1.l, 1.r) is in the 't' bank, row e. Side 2 (2.l, 2.r) is in the 'b' bank, row f. The image shows legs 2 columns apart (6/8, 11/13, 16/18, 21/23, 26/28), so I used those columns.

For each button, the left-column 't' strip carries the Arduino signal wire (row d) and the pulldown resistor (row a). The resistor's other end goes to the ground rail. The right-column 'b' strip is wired to the 5V rail with a short red jumper (row h). Pressing a button therefore takes the input pin HIGH. This matches the schematic.
Rail naming: 5V rail = tp, GND rail = bn (the rail next to the resistors). Rail hole numbers follow the nearest breadboard column in the image.
5V goes to the Leonardo 5V pin and GND to GND.1. The USB cable is not part of the parts list, so it is not modelled.
